    diagnostic_cached_normal_search_test.go:53: scale=0.25 magnitude=10000000000 angle=0.40000000000000002 delta=-1.0100000000000001e-06 distance=0.75000049523991263 point=maths.Vec{X:7.427565427945147e-07, Y:0, Z:-1.756784427648325e-06} cached=maths.Vec{X:0.38941834230865063, Y:0, Z:0.9210609940028852} nearest=maths.Vec{X:0.9210609940028852, Y:0, Z:-0.38941834230865063}

These are two valid pairs of open triangular faces, one in z=0 and a
nearby face in x=delta. The ray meets the z plane first. After a large
world translation, converting the rounded world hit back to local space
can put the query closer to the x plane. The ray-hit face is still z=0.

The fixed tests assert the rotated z-plane normal. They do not require
nearest-point rounding to fail on every other architecture. No private
mesh or landing state is corrupted; both meshes and groups use their
normal constructors, and the trace test obtains its landing from reach.

To reproduce the search, copy find_cached_normal_test.go into scene/shape,
run go test -count=1 -v -run
'^TestDiagnosticFindCachedNormalRoundingCases$' ./scene/shape,
then remove that temporary copy.
